headline: Bucket distinct values by their occurrence count
statement: Return the k most frequent distinct integers in nums, in any order. The input guarantees that the set of k selected values is unique. Achieve better than O(n log n) time.
constraints: The top-k answer set is unique
intuition: Frequencies range only from 1 to n, so they can index buckets directly. Sorting values is unnecessary: collecting buckets from highest frequency to lowest visits the most common values first.
approach: Count each value with a frequency map.
Place each distinct value in the bucket indexed by its count.
Visit buckets downward and append values until k are collected.
correctness: Every distinct value appears exactly once in the bucket matching its true frequency. Descending bucket traversal emits values in nonincreasing frequency order. Thus the first k values are precisely the k greatest frequencies; the guaranteed unique boundary makes their set unambiguous.
bruteForce: Count values, then sort all distinct values by descending count. This costs O(n+u log u) for u distinct values.

complexity.explanation: Counting, bucket construction, and bucket scanning are linear; n+1 bucket slots and u values are stored.

pitfalls: Return distinct values, not their counts.
Do not rely on value ordering.
Stop after k values even when an entire bucket contains more entries.
